summary: On an iPhone the public site's whole page could be swiped sideways, as if floating; three causes that could do it are closed.
details: Poking Nora is tapping her, often twice in quick succession, and a double tap on iOS zooms the page, after which it pans in every direction. Her places no longer double-tap zoom; pinch zoom still works.
The page as a whole refuses sideways scrolling, so an element that reaches past a phone's screen is cut off at its edge instead of letting the page float.

Pokes are listened for on her places themselves: iOS Safari turns a tap on a plain element into a click only for an element that is listening, so a poke from the window alone might never have reached her on an iPhone.
Her box in the air, while she hops between places, stays inside a layer the size of the screen.
limitations: No desktop engine reproduces the swipe, so which cause it was is unconfirmed until it is checked on an iPhone.
